mentions.name: Sunshine Optimist
mentions.description: A static website that calculates optimistic daylight milestones for any location, such as the first 5pm sunset or an hour of daylight gained since the winter solstice. It offers comparisons to the earliest sunset of the year and shortest day, delivers carefully considered optimistic messaging at all times of year (including after the summer solstice when daylight is being lost), and runs entirely in the browser with no ads, tracking, or LLMs.
mentions.problem: The author used to manually look up day lengths and sunset milestones for their own location, which limited sharing updates to their location and meant friends only benefited when they posted; they wanted anyone to be able to get an optimistic message and milestone at any time.
mentions.audience: Anyone dealing with the short days and early sunsets of winter; the author wanted a site anyone could visit at any time for an optimistic message and a milestone to look forward to.
mentions.source_excerpt:
This is something I built over the holidays to support people having a hard time with the short days and early sunsets: https://sunshineoptimist.com.

For the past several years I would look up the day lengths and sunset times for my location and identify milestones like “first 5pm sunset”, “1 hour of daylight gained since the winter solstice”, etc.
